events.title: China stockpiles gold at undisclosed rates
events.summary: According to Goldman Sachs estimates cited in the article, China acquired approximately 270 tonnes of physical gold in 2025, far exceeding officially reported purchases. China acquired roughly 10 tonnes in November (11 times official reports), 15 tonnes in September (10 times official reports), and 0.9 tonnes in December, marking the 14th consecutive month of purchases and bringing total gold reserves to a record 2,306 tonnes.
events.why_relevant: China's massive undisclosed gold accumulation suggests preparation for a potential shift in the global monetary system away from the dollar, potentially positioning the yuan as a gold-backed reserve currency and fundamentally altering the international financial order.
events.federal_nexus: China's gold purchases are a response to uncertainty about U.S. financial stability and policy under the Trump administration.
events.basis: China acquired +10 tonnes of gold in November, ~11 times more than officially reported by the central bank, according to Goldman Sachs estimates…Assuming official purchases were 10% of what China is actually buying, this suggests China acquired +270 tonnes of physical gold in 2025.

events.title: DEA finalizes rule registering emergency medical services agencies under Protecting Patient Access to Emergency Medications Act of 2017
events.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration published a final rule implementing the Protecting Patient Access to Emergency Medications Act of 2017, establishing a new registration category for emergency medical services (EMS) agencies that handle controlled substances. The rule codifies statutory amendments to the Controlled Substances Act, allowing EMS agencies to obtain a single registration per state, permits EMS personnel to administer controlled substances in schedules II–V outside direct medical director supervision pursuant to standing or verbal orders, and sets forth security, recordkeeping, and delivery requirements for controlled substance handling by EMS agencies. The rule becomes effective March 9, 2026.
events.why_relevant: This rule expands the authority of EMS personnel to administer controlled substances without direct physician oversight, fundamentally altering the regulatory framework governing emergency medical care and drug administration in the field.
